title: MASC: A Memory-Efficient Adjoint Sensitivity Analysis through Compression Using Novel Spatiotemporal Prediction
problem: Jacobian matrices generated during circuit transient analysis are too large to store in memory across multiple timesteps, requiring expensive disk I/O and limiting sensitivity analysis scalability. Computational complexity grows significantly with circuit size, number of objective functions, and simulation time points.
motivation: Adjoint sensitivity analysis is critical for modern IC design and verification, but its computational intensity and memory requirements constrain wider application.
method: The method reduces memory use by learning that Jacobian matrices (mathematical tables showing how circuit outputs respond to input changes) follow predictable patterns across time and space. It combines three techniques: sparse tensor representation using shared indices (storing only non-zero entries compactly), a spatiotemporal prediction model (forecasting future matrices based on learned time and space patterns), and residual encoding (recording only the small prediction errors). This keeps matrices in memory throughout forward transient analysis, eliminating the need for expensive disk I/O.
key_novelty: A spatiotemporal prediction model that learns how Jacobian matrices evolve across time steps and circuit regions, enabling compression by storing only prediction errors instead of complete matrices.
contributions: Memory-efficient compression achieving 16x average memory reduction for Jacobian matrices in circuit simulation
Shared-indices technique for sparse tensor compression exploiting matrix structure
Spatiotemporal prediction model capturing data patterns across time and space dimensions
Robust residual encoding scheme for efficient compression of prediction residuals
limitations: Specific baseline comparisons and design limitations not discussed in abstract.
primary_theme: Memory-efficient circuit simulation via spatiotemporal compression
